text:
anna-cs: FYI customer reports embeddings returning 403 after we provisioned a new service key. They say it worked with the demo key but not the tenant key. Repro steps below.

kelly-support: I reproduced in staging. Quick curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"hi"}'` -> 403 response: `{ "error": "forbidden", "missing": ["embeddings"] }`

anna-cs: Customer is on enterprise plan, urgent — they can’t index new docs.

jamie-platform: Pulled the issued JWT from the provisioner logs. Claim looks wrong: `claims.scopes = "inference,embeddings,rerank,"` (note the trailing comma).

devon-sre: That trailing comma is the smoking gun. APIGW split routine was updated to split on comma and then run a filter that accidentally drops the last non-empty item when an empty token follows a trailing comma (edge case in our split+reduce helper). Result: downstream receives scopes `inference,rerank` only.

rob-eng: Reproduced locally with provisioner v2.1.4 — it appends a comma when building the CSV list if scope_count > 1 and forgets to trim. Quick repro in node: `scopes = scopes.join(',') + ','` -> oops.

kelly-support: Customer provided a sample token. I patched it locally by trimming the claim and re-sent to APIGW; embeddings started working.

infra-bot: Created ticket CS-3338: "provisioner emits trailing-comma in scopes -> embeddings 403" assigned to jamie-platform,devon-sre severity=P2.

anna-cs: Customer asks ETA for a permanent fix and whether a rotation is required.

jamie-platform: I'm prepping a small hotfix to trim trailing commas at issuance and add a unit test. Will cut a release to staging today (ETA 3h) and prod tomorrow after smoke tests. Also adding a lint in the template builder to avoid emitting the trailing delimiter.

devon-sre: I'll add a defensive normalization at the APIGW layer so existing keys with the trailing comma continue to work: if `claims.scopes` contains a trailing delimiter, normalize to remove empty tokens before policy eval. That gives us zero-downtime mitigation.

rob-eng: For immediate remediation we can: 1) rotate the customer's key from console (fast) or 2) have APIGW normalization (safer for many tenants). Which do they prefer?

kelly-support: Customer prefers we avoid rotation while they ingest; they asked for the APIGW mitigation first. I confirmed mitigation works in staging (normalized variant allowed embeddings).

jamie-platform: I'll push the provisioner patch and include a backfill script to scan recently issued keys for trailing commas and rotate them in a controlled window. Will post PR link when ready.

devon-sre: Added small patch to APIGW ruleset: `if scopes_str.endswith(','): scopes_str = scopes_str.rstrip(',')` and then `scopes = [s for s in scopes_str.split(',') if s]` — behavior verified against the failing token.

anna-cs: Great. Assigning follow-ups: @jamie-platform hotfix+backfill, @devon-sre APIGW rule rollout, I'll update the customer with ETA and mitigation.

kelly-support: Customer updated: thanks for fast follow-up, they’ll wait for the APIGW rule to land in prod. Will confirm after we flip. :thumbsup:

jamie-platform: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/provisioner/pulls/1245 — adds trim + unit test. Rolling to staging now.

devon-sre: APIGW rule PR: https://git.internal/redwood/apigw/pulls/876 — added normalization + integration test. Planning staged rollout.

anna-cs: Closing loop: customer will validate after prod rollout. Keeping ticket open until we backfill keys and confirm no other tenants affected.

kelly-support: Noted. I’ll add postmortem blurb and update CS-3338 with customer confirmation when we get it.
